premise.claim: A CacheRuntime that names only limits.memory on a worker whose CacheRuntimeClass template declares a full set loses requests.cpu, requests.memory and limits.cpu from the workload on the next reconcile, with no error and no event; Claims is dropped the same way (issue #6173).
premise.evidence: Canary at merge base e0fc4c18: 'limits.cpu dropped (got "0")', 'requests dropped: got map[]', claims dropped at both creation and sync layers — results/unit-base.log

integration.cmd: FLUID_UNIT_TEST=true go test ./pkg/ddc/cache/engine/ -run TestCacheEngine -ginkgo.focus "names part of the template's resources" -ginkgo.json-report=$GINKGO_REPORT -v

match: should move the key it names and keep the template's other requirements
should leave requests unset and stop patching once converged

findings.note: delta c1c303e8..e259d738: desiredComponentResources never returns nil; a key neither side declares is cleared. fails on c1c303e (nil return), passes on e259d738.

F6 fixed by commit f02054bd (round 3): the canary flipped, so it was inverted into a contract test — the sync must refuse the conflicting merge, leave the workload's resources untouched and emit a RuntimeResourcesConflict Warning event.
delta made the tiered-store quota read-back unconditional: an unconstrained container with a memory tmpfs must stay unconstrained and unpatched.
round 3: the conflict must not abort the component sync — replicas still move while the resource patch is skipped and the Warning event names the memory pair.
round 3: the creation path (transformWorker) must fail loudly on a conflicting pair, naming the component and the keys, instead of rendering a pod spec the API server rejects at rollout.
round 3: the master call site in syncRuntimeSpec shares the worker's validation; pin the skip + event + replica behavior there too.

round 4 (497bbeaf..3adc547d): the non-overcommittable family rules. D7/D8 fail on 497bbeaf (rules absent) and pass on 3adc547d (commit 3adc547d adds isOvercommitAllowed + the equality/no-limit rules, verified verbatim against k8s.io/kubernetes@v1.29.15 pkg/apis/core/v1/helper/helpers.go and validation.go:6568-6578). Kept as regression contracts.

round 6 (ce4f0c4f..a773dfa6): FIXED by a773dfa6 — splitDeclaredClaims + validDesiredResources(podSpec) drop container claims the workload does not declare (pod-level or already carried), emit a RuntimeResourcesConflict Warning naming them, and still sync the rest. E1 contract: fail at ce4f0c4f (round-5 log), pass at a773dfa6 (results/round6/). B3 stays green (no over-drop). Remedy matches the F6/F9 guard pattern proposed in round 4.

refutation record for Copilot discussion_r4212708077 ('empty resource maps fail to clear workload limits'): an explicit limits:{} still clears the workload's stale limit; the contract passes on base, 497bbeaf and 3adc547d. Copilot's claim that desiredComponentResources 'returns nil' does not match the code — it never returns nil.

round 5 (3adc547d..ce4f0c4f): fixed by 94121e27 — syncRuntimeSpec guards a topology-less class before the first dereference. D9 FAILS (panic) on 3adc547d and PASSES on ce4f0c4f. getRuntimeClass still rejects such classes up front, so this stays defense in depth.

round 5: coverage fixed by 44e6c90a + ce4f0c4f (the equivalence table renders tiered-store rows and pins the charged quota). D10 is a regression PIN, not a flip: it passes on both heads; the PR's own new specs are the coverage fix, D10 keeps the creation/sync quota agreement pinned in this harness.

round 5: fixed by 71d94397 + 4a8668f9 — the creation path routes validation through checkComponentResources, which emits the RuntimeResourcesConflict Warning event. D11 FAILS on 3adc547d (error, no event) and PASSES on ce4f0c4f. Worker call site driven; master and client share the wrapper and are covered by the PR's own specs.
